_comment: Which compilers may build this project, and where the tree still names ones that may not.

INV-7 says a board enters the matrix only if the house toolchain builds it, so 'which compiler' is a contract, not a detail: the same source compiled by two foundations produces two sets of evidence that cannot be compared.

This file is the data half; toolchain_gate.py is the teeth half. T1 scans the surface we own for third-party compiler names, T2 refuses a debt entry without why/exit, T3 refuses a stale debt entry (the literal it claims is no longer in the file).
哪些编译器可以构建本工程，以及树里还在指名哪些不行的。INV-7 规定'板子进矩阵的前提是 house 工具链能构建它'，所以'用哪个编译器'是合同而不是细节：同一份源码由两套地基编出来，是两套无法互相比较的证据。
本文件是数据那一半，toolchain_gate.py 是牙齿那一半：T1 扫我们自己的面里有没有第三方编译器名，T2 拒收没有 why/exit 的债务条目，T3 拒收已失效的债务条目（它声称的字面量在文件里已不存在）。
T1 只扫**代码面**（.py/.sh/.json/.yml/.c/.h/.cpp）：规矩是「我们的脚本不许调用第三方编译器」，而文档/笔记**可以**提这些名字——本文件和 gaps.md 就在讨论禁令本身。
T4 每块板型必须指名一个已申报的 house 包，且它的 triplet 必须是该包真正提供的目标；板型本身就是一个声称（m33 那次为一个错的 profile 花了一天），所以它必须与工具链表一致，而不是自己发明一个编译器。
T5 CI 跑不动的重活仍然是**一等公民**：命令、所需 profile、在哪跑、为什么不在 CI 跑。只活在某个人的 shell 历史里的重活，和没人跑的门禁是同一种病。

arm-toolchain/11.3.rel1.resolved_by: declared version probe against the Conan cache (.github/project/qa/kat/run_kat.py: find_tool)
arm-toolchain/11.3.rel1.why: the four Cortex-M boards, the two ARM Linux userspace boards and every ARM variant are built by it

rv-toolchain/14.3.rel1.resolved_by: same probe mechanism; xpack reports GCC 14.2.0
rv-toolchain/14.3.rel1.why: PLAN 3.3 pins the RV mainline to 14.3.rel1 (ratified RVV 1.0 headers need GCC >= 13)

skip_dirs.why: vendored upstream sources used for parity (tflite-micro / CMSIS-NN / XNNPACK / llama.cpp …): their CI is not our surface and we never run it, so their compiler names are not a drift we own

heavy_checks.runs_from: preflight, or any machine that has the house profiles; measured green on 2026-11-26 for both profiles
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: the project-gates job has no conan, no house profiles and no warm cache, so running it there would be red for reasons that have nothing to do with the tree

heavy_checks.runs_from: preflight, or any machine with the house toolchains and qemu; measured green 2026-11-26 (6 builds pass, 6 skip with reasons)
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: the project-gates job has no Conan cache, no house cross toolchain and no qemu, so it would be red for reasons that have nothing to do with the tree; T5 keeps this declaration honest and located

heavy_checks.runs_from: preflight, or any machine with the house toolchains and qemu; measured green 2026-11-26
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: the project-gates job has none of the cross toolchains and no qemu, so the chains would be red for reasons that have nothing to do with the tree; the evidence index cites this id, so an undeclared check would be a claim with no footing

heavy_checks.runs_from: host-native: no cross profile is involved, so 'host' is the whole requirement; measured 2026-11-27 on this box producing a 290 KB ONNX graph from mobilenet_v3_small
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: torch is ~200 MB of wheels that exist to *author* a model, and the project-gates job has no such env -- what CI needs is the ONNX file and the tensors, which are what the export produces. Declared here so the dependency is visible instead of living in a shell history (T5), and so Y5 keeps it out of ci.sh

heavy_checks.runs_from: any machine with a host toolchain and a clean (non-gcov) build of the library; see .github/project/qa/measure/README.md for the object build loop
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: it links a hand-built object set rather than the Conan package (the packaged archive carries gcov counters that distort timings) and its verdict is a throughput ratio, which is a measurement and not a pass/fail

heavy_checks.runs_from: any machine with torch, torchvision, onnx and pyyaml; no network needed (random weights, same operator set)
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: torch and onnx are machine-level tooling and are not in the project's dependency buckets; the census is a design input, not a gate

heavy_checks.runs_from: same as tier-ab plus xnnpack/cci.20241203, pthreadpool and cpuinfo from the Conan cache
heavy_checks.why_not_in_ci: needs the XNNPACK package and a hand-built clean object set, and it answers a comparison question rather than asserting an invariant

debt.why: template-owned workflow: its cross-compile job apt-installs gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu / gcc-arm-none-eabi, so the CI cross-compile leg and the local KAT matrix are two different foundations (apt 13.x vs house 11.3.rel1)
debt.exit: authorised scaffold edit: build through the house toolchain (conan install -pr armv8 / -pr armv7hf) and drop the apt step; or delete the job once the KAT matrix covers the same ground

debt.why: template-owned helper: its toolchain table hardcodes apt package names and compiler binaries
debt.exit: authorised scaffold edit: resolve from the Conan cache by version probe, the same way run_kat.py does

debt.why: template-owned benchmark driver: it reaches for system cross compilers when it runs the on-board bench
debt.exit: authorised scaffold edit, or keep it and state in the release notes that the bench path (never the shipped library) uses a host compiler
